traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Rule file `src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts` implements the core "annotation format validation" behavior described in the story. - It validates @story, @req, and @implements annotations by scanning all comments in the file inside the `Program` visitor, via `processComment` and `processCommentLine`. - `validateStoryAnnotation`: - Trims and collapses multi-line values using `collapseAnnotationValue`. - Validates the story path against a configurable regex (`options.storyPattern`), enforcing the expected path shape (e.g. `docs/stories/... .story.md`). - Detects missing values and reports with `messageId: "invalidStoryFormat"` and detailed messages produced by `buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", ...)`. - Detects invalid formats (including invalid suffixes, whitespace issues, and non-matching paths) and reports with `invalidStoryFormat` and details from `buildStoryErrorMessage("invalid", collapsed, options)`. - Attempts safe, minimal auto-fixes for missing/incorrect suffixes using `getFixedStoryPath` and `createStoryFix`, while preserving surrounding comment formatting, via `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix`. - `validateReqAnnotation`: - Trims and collapses values with `collapseAnnotationValue`. - Validates requirement IDs against `options.reqPattern` (defaulting to a REQ-* format pattern) and reports `invalidReqFormat` with detailed messages from `buildReqErrorMessage` for missing or invalid IDs. - `processComment` and `processCommentLine` provide multi-line support and flexible parsing: - `normalizeCommentLine` strips leading `*` and comment syntax to allow different JSDoc and line-comment styles. - Maintains a `PendingAnnotation` structure across lines for @story/@req, appending continuation lines and collapsing whitespace (supports annotations split across multiple lines). - Starts a new pending annotation when detecting `@story` or `@req`, finalizes and validates pending ones via `finalizePendingAnnotation`. - Treats `@implements` as a single-line annotation and validates it immediately via `validateImplementsAnnotation`, which delegates to `validateImplementsAnnotationHelper` with dependencies (`MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS`, `reportMissingImplementsReqIds`, `reportInvalidImplementsStoryPath`, etc.). This enforces the `@implements [...]` format. - Error messaging: - `meta.messages.invalidStoryFormat`, `invalidReqFormat`, and `invalidImplementsFormat` all use a shared pattern: `"Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."`, satisfying the requirement for clear, specific, and consistent errors. Details include the offending value and an example of the expected format. - `invalidRuleConfiguration` reports configuration issues for custom regex patterns without stopping validation (`"Invalid configuration for valid-annotation-format: {{details}}"`), enabling safe fallback behavior. - Configuration / quality: - Uses `getRuleSchema()` for rule options schema (ESLint best practices). - Uses `resolveOptions` and `getOptionErrors` from `./helpers/valid-annotation-options` to handle configurable regex patterns for story paths and requirement IDs, with explicit handling of invalid regex patterns and fallback to defaults. - Rule is declared as `type: "problem"`, `recommended: "error"`, and `fixable: "code"`, matching typical ESLint rule conventions. - Traceability: - The rule and its helpers are annotated with references to `docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` and related stories, and requirements like `REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION`, `REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION`, `REQ-PATH-FORMAT`, `REQ-REQ-FORMAT`, `REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT`, `REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING`, and `REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY` in JSDoc and inline comments.
Tests: - Test file `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` explicitly references this story: - Header: - `* Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Verify valid-annotation-format rule enforces annotation format syntax` - `describe("Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)", () => { ... })` clearly scopes the suite to this story. - The `valid` test cases cover all main requirements: - `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] valid story annotation format (single-line)` with `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`. - `[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] valid req annotation format (single-line)` with `// @req REQ-EXAMPLE`. - `[REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION] valid block annotations (single-line values)` with combined @story/@req in a block comment. - `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT]` cases where @story and @req values span multiple lines inside a block comment, verifying that collapsing whitespace produces a valid path/ID. - `[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING] valid JSDoc-style comment with leading stars and spacing`, confirming tolerance of varying whitespace and JSDoc formatting. - Additional valid cases confirm support for configurable patterns and examples (used by later stories), but also demonstrate that format validation is driven by regex options. - The `invalid` test cases thoroughly exercise format violations listed in the story: - `// @story` (missing path) with expected details: `Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md".` - Story paths missing `.story.md` extension or having wrong extension: - `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story` with an auto-fix to `.story.md` and detailed error message. - `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION` similarly fixed and reported. - Path traversal: - `// @story ../docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` reported invalid, matching the story’s requirement to disallow `../` traversal. - @req issues: - `// @req` (missing identifier) with specific details: `Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "REQ-EXAMPLE".` - `// @req invalid-format` and `// @req ` (trailing space, no ID) producing detailed `invalidReqFormat` errors, including echo of the offending ID and example format. - Multi-line error cases: - Block comment with `@story` but no path lines following. - Multi-line story path that collapses to an invalid suffix. - Multi-line @req with an invalid collapsed ID (e.g. `invalid- format`). - Error messages are asserted exactly (via `details` strings), verifying **REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY** and the story's requirement for clear, actionable messages. - Multi-line and continuation logic: - Tests such as `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT] valid multi-line @story annotation value in block comment` and `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT] invalid multi-line story path after collapsing whitespace` confirm that annotations split over multiple lines are correctly concatenated and validated. - Flexible parsing: - JSDoc-style and spacing variations are covered, confirming **REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING**. - The test suite uses helper factories `makeInvalid` and `makeInvalidStory` to consistently assert `messageId` and `data.details`, ensuring alignment with the implementation’s error-reporting structure.
Execution evidence: - The following targeted test command was executed: - `npm test -- --verbose --runTestsByPath tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` - Command output (captured): - `> eslint-plugin-traceability@1.0.5 test` - `> jest --ci --bail --verbose --runTestsByPath tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` - No errors or failures were reported by the tool wrapper, indicating that the `valid-annotation-format` rule tests ran without test-runner errors.
Story alignment by requirement: - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION: The combination of `valid-annotation-format.ts` implementation, its use of `storyPattern`/`reqPattern` regexes, and the comprehensive valid/invalid test cases define and enforce clear annotation format rules. - REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: `processComment`, `processCommentLine`, and `finalizePendingAnnotation` detect missing/invalid values and dispatch to `validateStoryAnnotation` / `validateReqAnnotation`, which enforce the spec and report precise errors. Tests cover missing values, invalid delimiters, and continuation syntax. - REQ-PATH-FORMAT: `validateStoryAnnotation` and supporting helpers enforce the required path structure and disallow path traversal; the tests assert correct behavior for missing extensions, wrong extensions, and `../` paths. - REQ-REQ-FORMAT: `validateReqAnnotation` validates identifiers against a strict pattern and reports missing/invalid IDs with example formats; tests cover multiple failure modes. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: The `PendingAnnotation` model and the line-processing logic allow values to span multiple lines; both valid and invalid multi-line scenarios are covered by tests. - REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: `normalizeCommentLine` and the regex checks handle various comment styles and whitespace; JSDoc-formatted examples and differently spaced annotations in tests confirm this. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: Error messages include the offending path/ID and a concrete example of the expected format; tests assert the exact `details` strings for each violation.
Acceptance criteria mapping: - Core Functionality: The `valid-annotation-format` ESLint rule validates `@story` and `@req` (and `@implements`) annotation format and syntax, with extensive tests in `valid-annotation-format.test.ts`. - Quality Standards: The rule follows ESLint best practices (meta schema, `messages`, `type: "problem"`, `recommended: "error"`, `fixable: "code"`, and structured options handling). - Integration: It operates over all comments in the AST and validates annotations produced by the same comment-level annotations used by the function/branch rules, and is referenced in the test/traceability annotations alongside other rules, demonstrating its role in the overall validation pipeline. - User Experience: Errors are consistent, specific, and include actionable guidance and examples, with tests confirming the exact phrasings. - Error Handling: Guards for missing tags/values, invalid regex patterns, and multi-line structures ensure graceful handling of malformed comments and configuration, all verified by tests (including configuration-error cases). - Documentation: The story itself contains format examples of valid and invalid annotations; the rule and tests include JSDoc comments with references to this story and requirement IDs, serving as a living, executable format specification.
